note: The corpus both implementations of doc-lint are run against.
create-react-app (and the other Node scaffolders) are the same nine-rule
linter written twice, in two languages, against two dependency manifests
(pubspec.yaml for Flutter, package.json for Node). Two implementations of
one contract drift; these cases are what stops them drifting silently.
Each case names a tree of files written to a temp dir before the linter
runs. Both implementations run against the same bytes; `violations[].rule`
and `violations[].match` are the contract — `match` is the substring that
must appear in the rejection message, deliberately a phrase both
implementations word identically, so the prose can still improve on
either side without breaking the corpus.
The corpus exercises both manifest shapes — pubspec.yaml and package.json —
so the Flutter-only path and the Node-parity path are both pinned. D6
fires for both; the corpus uses one of each so a rule added to one
manifest and forgotten in the other goes red on both.

cases.why: The shape both dialects agree is a harnessed Flutter project: four entry files inside budget, prelude inside budget, one constraint each that names its consequence, a feature the register can point at and the evidence file the rule D9 expects.
